episode.title: Deny argument-restricted shell commands when parsing is unreliable in automatic-approval mode
episode.before: At parent cfd7541ad45b25109744c988ac5fc8128accb0ec, shell-command checking treated only an empty parsed-command list as a parsing failure. When approval mode was YOLO, that failure path returned ALLOW after preserving an explicit DENY, even when the matched ALLOW rule had an argsPattern whose argument restrictions could not be validated. A parser result with nonempty details and hasError=true did not enter the failure path.
episode.after: At ed469e492b4190ce8983b9dd1c5fb5b9f1b140d0, either an empty parsed-command list or parsed.hasError enters the parsing-failure path. In YOLO mode, a matched rule carrying argsPattern now forces DENY because its argument restriction cannot be validated; rules without argument restrictions retain the existing YOLO ALLOW behavior, explicit DENY remains DENY, and non-YOLO failures still fall back to the configured default decision.
episode.diff: The policy engine broadened the unreliable-parse predicate from subCommands.length === 0 to subCommands.length === 0 || parsed?.hasError, then inserted a YOLO-mode guard that returns DENY when the matched rule has argsPattern before retaining ALLOW for unrestricted rules. Two unit tests mock parseCommandDetails for (1) empty details with hasError=true and (2) nonempty details with hasError=true, and assert DENY for a matching argument-restricted ALLOW rule.

evidence_units.claim: Commit ed469e492b4190ce8983b9dd1c5fb5b9f1b140d0 resolves PR/issue 25935 with the subject 'fix(core): fail closed in YOLO mode when shell parsing fails for restricted rules' and has parent cfd7541ad45b25109744c988ac5fc8128accb0ec.
evidence_units.source: git show --format=fuller ed469e492b4190ce8983b9dd1c5fb5b9f1b140d0; issue-bundle.json linked_pull_requests[0].commits[0] and parent_commit

evidence_units.claim: In the parent implementation, an empty parse result preserved explicit DENY but returned ALLOW in YOLO mode without checking whether the matched rule had an argument pattern.
The parent failure predicate checked only subCommands.length === 0, so a parser result with nonempty details and hasError=true continued through ordinary subcommand validation.
evidence_units.source: git show cfd7541ad45b25109744c988ac5fc8128accb0ec:packages/core/src/policy/policy-engine.ts, checkShellCommand immediately after parseCommandDetails

evidence_units.claim: The change treats empty details or parsed.hasError as unreliable parsing and, in YOLO mode, returns DENY when the matched rule has argsPattern while retaining ALLOW when no argument restriction applies.

When a shell tool call matches a policy rule, PolicyEngine.check passes the command, derived rule decision, and the matched rule into checkShellCommand, making the rule's argsPattern available to the new guard.
When no policy rule matches, PolicyEngine.check invokes checkShellCommand with rule undefined; the new argsPattern guard therefore does not alter YOLO's unrestricted no-match ALLOW behavior.
A unit test mocks parsing of 'echo bypass' to return empty details with hasError=true and verifies that a matching argument-restricted ALLOW rule produces DENY in YOLO mode.
evidence_units.source: git show ed469e492b4190ce8983b9dd1c5fb5b9f1b140d0:packages/core/src/policy/policy-engine.test.ts, test 'should fail closed in YOLO mode when shell parsing fails for restricted rule'

evidence_units.claim: A unit test mocks parsing of 'echo bypass' to return an echo detail together with hasError=true and verifies that the same argument-restricted ALLOW rule produces DENY in YOLO mode.
evidence_units.source: git show ed469e492b4190ce8983b9dd1c5fb5b9f1b140d0:packages/core/src/policy/policy-engine.test.ts, test 'should fail closed in YOLO mode when shell parsing has errors for restricted rule'

evidence_units.claim: Existing adjacent tests establish that YOLO mode still allows by default when no rule matches and does not override an explicit DENY rule.
evidence_units.source: git show ed469e492b4190ce8983b9dd1c5fb5b9f1b140d0:packages/core/src/policy/policy-engine.test.ts, tests 'should return ALLOW by default in YOLO mode when no rules match' and 'should NOT override explicit DENY rules in YOLO mode'

evidence_units.claim: The committed regression oracle covers both representations of unreliable parsing relevant to the implementation predicate: no parsed command details and parsed details accompanied by a parser error flag; both must return DENY for an argument-restricted rule in YOLO mode.
evidence_units.source: packages/core/src/policy/policy-engine.test.ts at ed469e492b4190ce8983b9dd1c5fb5b9f1b140d0; two added regression tests

candidate_atomics.name: deny_restricted_effect_when_validation_parse_is_unreliable
candidate_atomics.title: Deny a restricted effect when its arguments cannot be reliably parsed
candidate_atomics.description: At an automatic-approval boundary, classify empty or error-bearing parser output as unreliable and deny an otherwise allowed effect when the matched policy depends on argument-level restrictions that can no longer be validated, while preserving behavior for explicit denials and unrestricted approvals.

semantic_action.intent: Prevent an automatic-approval mode from bypassing argument-level policy constraints when effect arguments cannot be parsed reliably.
semantic_action.module_role: effect authorization boundary that reconciles parser confidence with matched policy restrictions
semantic_action.pre_state: An effect request is being evaluated in automatic-approval mode; a matched rule would allow it but carries an argument restriction, and parsing yields either no usable command details or an error-bearing result.
semantic_action.post_state: The request is denied whenever argument-restricted authorization cannot be validated from reliable parse output; explicit denials remain denied, while unrestricted automatic approvals remain eligible for ALLOW.
semantic_action.validation: Mock both empty/error and nonempty/error parser results for a request matching an argument-restricted ALLOW rule and assert DENY; retain adjacent tests proving default unrestricted YOLO ALLOW and explicit DENY behavior.
parameters: effect request and raw argument string

candidate_workflows.name: fail_closed_when_restricted_effect_arguments_cannot_be_validated
candidate_workflows.title: Fail closed when restricted effect arguments cannot be validated
candidate_workflows.description: Harden an automatic effect-approval path by coupling parser reliability to argument-restricted authorization: unreliable parsing blocks only approvals whose safety depends on inspecting parsed arguments, with focused regression coverage for each failure representation and preserved behavior for unrelated policy branches.

workflow_graph.goal: Ensure automatic approval cannot execute an effect under an argument-restricted rule when parser output is insufficient or internally marked erroneous.
when_to_use: An automatic or non-interactive approval path authorizes effects using constraints on parsed arguments.
The parser can return no details or can return partial details together with an error indicator.
Proceeding after parse failure would prevent the policy engine from validating the restriction that justified approval.
anti_goals: Do not convert every parser failure into a blanket denial when no argument-level restriction must be validated.
Do not override an explicit DENY decision.
Do not change normal successful-parse evaluation, redirection handling, rule priority, or unrelated heuristic behavior.
not_applicable_when: Authorization does not depend on parsed argument structure or values.
Parser output is reliable and ordinary policy validation can complete.
The desired contract explicitly permits unrestricted execution despite parse failure and no restrictive rule matched.
inputs: effect request containing the raw command or argument string
matched policy rule and decision, if any
parser result containing details and an error indicator
workflow_graph.entry_state: Automatic approval can return ALLOW after unreliable parsing even though the matched approval rule contains an argument restriction that cannot be validated.
workflow_graph.exit_state: Unreliable parser output causes DENY for matched argument-restricted approvals, while explicit denials, unrestricted automatic approvals, non-automatic fallback behavior, and successful parsing retain their established semantics.

steps.condition: Apply when automatic approval is active, parsing yields zero usable details or reports an error, and the matched rule contains an argument restriction.
steps.validation: The empty-details/error and nonempty-details/error regression cases both return DENY; existing default-ALLOW and explicit-DENY YOLO cases remain intact.

validation_ladder: Inspect the parent implementation to confirm the bypass: empty parse output returns ALLOW in automatic-approval mode without considering argument restrictions, and nonempty error-bearing output is not classified as failure.
Verify the implementation predicate recognizes both absent details and the parser error flag, and that the restrictive-rule guard precedes the unrestricted automatic-ALLOW return.
Run or inspect focused unit cases for empty/error and partial/error parse results under a matched argument-restricted ALLOW rule; each oracle is DENY.
Run or inspect adjacent policy-engine tests confirming no-match automatic approval remains ALLOW and explicit DENY remains DENY.
stop_conditions: Stop if the matched policy has no argument restriction; this episode does not justify denying that unrestricted automatic-approval branch.
Stop if parsing is reliable; continue through the existing detailed policy evaluation instead of applying the failure guard.
Defer extraction if the parser has no observable reliability signal and no test can force the relevant failure states.
unresolved_or_deferred: The GitHub bundle does not include PR discussion, reviews, or status-check results.
No test execution result was available from the inspected checkout state; validation is grounded in the committed unit-test oracles rather than a recorded local test run.
Behavior for parser failures under other approval modes was intentionally preserved and is not newly characterized beyond the implementation fallback path.

unresolved_questions: Was the focused policy-engine test suite executed successfully in CI for this commit? The evidence bundle omits status checks and the extraction found no recorded execution result.

Are there additional parser failure representations beyond empty details and hasError=true that should be treated as unreliable? The inspected change and tests establish only these two representations.
